html:
In 1952 Eritrea was joined to Ethiopia as a self-governing unit in a federation set up by the United Nations, and in 1962 Emperor Haile Selassie ended the federation and annexed it.

After British rule from 1941, Eritreans were split between union with Ethiopia and independence. The United Nations chose federation, with Eritrea keeping its own parliament, flag and languages. Under pressure from Haile Selassie, Tigrinya and Arabic were pushed aside for Amharic, parties were banned and the press was closed.

In November 1962 the Eritrean assembly voted to dissolve itself, under Ethiopian pressure, and Eritrea became a province. Armed resistance had already begun in 1961, and the annexation turned it into the Eritrean War of Independence.
sum: In 1952 Eritrea was joined to Ethiopia as a self-governing unit in a federation set up by the United Nations, and in 1962 Emperor Haile Selassie ended the federation and annexed it.
